top_stories.title: IDScan sued over alleged data breach affecting 153 million drivers
top_stories.summary: Identity verification company IDScan faces multiple lawsuits after hackers allegedly breached its systems and offered to sell data from more than 153 million driver's licenses. The breach targets a company whose core business is identity document scanning and verification, a critical component of identity proofing workflows.

top_stories.title: 39 New Methods That Compromise Passkey Authentication
top_stories.summary: Researchers have documented 39 methods for compromising passkey-based authentication systems without breaking FIDO2 cryptography. The attack vectors include abuse of authentication prompts, synced credentials, enrollment processes, recovery mechanisms, and other trust boundaries.

top_stories.title: Impersonating IT support: how threat actors turn a remote session into enterprise-wide access
top_stories.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence documented a human-operated attack campaign that exploits Microsoft Teams external collaboration features to impersonate IT support personnel and gain unauthorized remote access to enterprise systems. Attackers use social engineering via Teams to convince users to grant remote sessions, then deploy a Node.js-based implant to establish persistence and move laterally across the environment.

top_stories.title: New identity governance and access features in Microsoft Entra
top_stories.summary: Microsoft released multiple generally available and preview updates to Microsoft Entra in September 2026, covering identity governance and access management capabilities. The updates include tenant governance, user-centric access reviews, lifecycle workflow management, passwordless Teams device identities, and hybrid identity features.

top_stories.title: Attackers Pounce on Critical Artifactory Bug Following Disclosure
top_stories.summary: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-82329) has been disclosed in JFrog Artifactory, allowing attackers to gain administrative-level access on affected systems. Threat actors are actively exploiting the flaw following its public disclosure.

news.title: Critical Citrix NetScaler auth bypass now leveraged in attacks
news.summary: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability in Citrix NetScaler (CVE-2026-19490) is being actively exploited in the wild. The flaw allows attackers to bypass authentication controls, with exploitation confirmed by vulnerability intelligence firm Previdian.

news.title: Microsoft Teams is about to make QR code phishing much harder
news.summary: Microsoft is developing a new Teams feature that will automatically hide QR codes sent by external users, requiring recipients to manually reveal them before viewing or scanning. The feature is expected to roll out in October 2026 across Android, desktop, iOS, and Mac platforms.

news.title: A five-part inventory for your AI agent credentials
news.summary: Roy Katmor, CEO of Orchid, outlines a five-part inventory framework for managing AI agent credentials that fall outside standard identity review processes. The framework addresses how AI agents built in studios receive accounts and access to enterprise tools—including HR systems, identity providers, ticketing, and payroll—without being subject to normal identity governance reviews.

news.title: New infosec products of the week: September 4, 2026
news.summary: A weekly product roundup covers new releases from BugBase, F5 Networks, Ping Identity, and Superna. The Ping Identity inclusion makes it marginally relevant to IAM professionals, though the article is a broad infosec product digest rather than focused IAM coverage.

news.title: Your Employee’s Password Appeared in an Infostealer Log. Now What?
news.summary: Flare published guidance on responding to employee credential exposure in infostealer logs, covering risks beyond passwords such as stolen authenticated sessions that can bypass MFA. The article outlines how defenders can prioritize compromised identities and assess whether stolen access remains valid to prevent account takeover.

news.title: Thomson Reuters Court Software Breach May Have Exposed SSNs and Sealed Data
news.summary: Thomson Reuters disclosed a breach of C-Track, its court case management platform, in which an unauthorized party obtained files affecting courts in 11 U.S. states, the U.S. Virgin Islands, and Ontario, Canada. The breach, discovered June 30, 2026, potentially exposed sensitive personal data including Social Security Numbers and sealed court records.

news.title: Shai-Hulud's Reach Just Grew to 469 Credential Locations. Here's What That Means
news.summary: GitGuardian researchers discovered a new variant of the Shai-Hulud infostealer worm that scans for credentials across 469 locations, up from 189 in earlier variants. The expanded targeting covers developer environments, CI/CD tooling, cloud configurations, and AI tool configs.

news.title: Researcher Releases FalconFlank PoC Showing Privilege Escalation in CrowdStrike Falcon
news.summary: A security researcher released a proof-of-concept exploit called FalconFlank demonstrating a privilege escalation zero-day vulnerability in CrowdStrike Falcon Sensor. The flaw abuses the office malicious macros remediation feature within the Falcon Sensor to achieve privilege escalation.

news.title: Microsoft Security enhancements: Defender MDR Plan 2, Entra Tenant Governance, Intune Autopilot, Purview Auto-Labeling, and AI Agent Containment
news.summary: Microsoft has announced a set of security enhancements including Entra Tenant Governance for multi-tenant identity governance management. Additional updates include Defender MDR Plan 2 support for third-party logs, Intune Autopilot improvements, Purview auto-labeling throughput increases, and AI agent containment guidance.

news.title: An infostealer log can bypass MFA—respond within the first hour
news.summary: Research highlights that infostealer logs can contain active browser session cookies and identity-provider tokens that allow attackers to bypass MFA entirely. Security teams are advised to treat corporate credentials found in infostealer logs as potential live identity compromises requiring response within the first hour to revoke sessions before attackers can exploit them.

news.title: The $100M Signal: Why AI Agent Security is Becoming Its Own Category
news.summary: The article discusses the emergence of AI agent security as a distinct security category, driven by the shift from simple chatbots to autonomous AI agents that can execute tasks, access data, and make decisions on behalf of users. The piece addresses how traditional identity and access management approaches are challenged by AI agents requiring new frameworks for authorization, authentication, and access control.

news.title: Keeper Security Names Jessica Krowel and Bill Grabner to Lead North America Private and Public Sector Sales
news.summary: Keeper Security appointed Jessica Krowel and Bill Grabner to lead North America private and public sector sales, respectively. The hires are described as strengthening the company's go-to-market team following Keeper's recognition as the second fastest-growing security software company globally.

news.title: Back to the Future: Why Agentic AI Needs a Strong Identity Foundation
news.summary: The article examines the identity infrastructure requirements for agentic AI deployments in enterprise environments. It addresses how AI agents require a strong identity foundation to manage authentication, authorization, and access controls as organizations scale automation use cases.

news.title: Old, Unpatched Flaws Give Attackers Access to Philippines Nuclear Agency
news.summary: Threat actors exploited unpatched vulnerabilities in ownCloud to breach the Philippines Nuclear Research Institute, stealing reactor databases, personnel records, and credential stores. The attack leveraged commodity vulnerabilities to gain initial access, resulting in the compromise of sensitive credential data.

news.title: Attackers Exploit Two SonicWall SMA 1000 Zero-Days That May Form an Attack Chain
news.summary: SonicWall has released security updates addressing two zero-day vulnerabilities in its Secure Mobile Access (SMA) 1000 series VPN appliances, including a critical pre-authentication SSRF flaw rated CVSS 10.0. The vulnerabilities, which may form an attack chain, have been actively exploited and were discovered internally by SonicWall researchers William Perry and Adam Babis.

news.title: A Beginner's Deep Dive Guide to Entra Passkeys
news.summary: The article provides a detailed guide on implementing passkeys in Microsoft Entra as a phishing-resistant authentication method. The content covers Entra passkey configuration and positions passkeys as a passwordless, phishing-resistant alternative to traditional passwords.

news.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
news.summary: A dark web service is selling digital scans of over 153 million U.S. and Canadian driver's licenses, apparently sourced from a Louisiana-based identity verification company. The FBI's New Orleans field office has launched an official inquiry into the breach, which directly implicates an identity verification provider's data security.

news.title: Anthropic Users Hit by Infostealer Attacks, Session Thefts
news.summary: A threat actor deployed infostealer malware to steal session tokens and gain unauthorized access to Claude (Anthropic) user accounts. The attack involved session hijacking techniques to bypass authentication on an unknown number of compromised accounts.

news.title: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty in Snowflake Extortions
news.summary: Canadian man Connor Riley Moucka pleaded guilty to computer fraud and conspiracy charges for hacking and extorting over 165 organizations using Snowflake cloud storage. The attacks involved stolen credentials used to access Snowflake customer accounts, resulting in data theft including over 100 million AT&T customer records.

news.title: Lessons Learned from CISA’s Recent GitHub Leak
news.summary: CISA issued a postmortem report after a contractor exposed dozens of internal credentials, including AWS GovCloud keys, in a public GitHub repository for nearly six months. The incident highlights credential management and secrets governance failures, with the leak only discovered after KrebsOnSecurity notified the agency.
